newsitem.title: USA: NYPA sees Indian Point nuke back later this week.
newsitem.headline: NYPA sees Indian Point nuke back later this week.

text.p: The New York Power Authority (NYPA) said Tuesday its 965 megawatt (MW) Indian Point nuclear unit 3 likely would begin delivering electricity to the grid later this week.
"We expect it to be later this week," said Joe Leary, an onsite spokesman, when asked about an on line schedule.
The unit along the Hudson River north of New York City was originally shut January 18 to repair its feedwater heaters.
The utility decided to extend the outage to repair the unit's power-operated relief valves and to reseal the manway to reactor coolant system.
Nuclear Regulatory Commission, in its daily status report Tuesday showed the unit would restart Wednesday.
Leary declined to provide a specific restart date.

The adjacent 975 MW Indian Point 2, operated by Consolidated Edison Co of New York, is expected to resume operation by early next week after being shut January 27 to correct problems that caused the feedwater valve to become inoperable.
